name: Glide
summary: No-code app builder, now sold as Glide Classic next to the newer GlideOS, that turns spreadsheets and databases into working business apps: internal tools, client portals and field apps, with workflows and an API.
best_for: teams that already run operations out of spreadsheets and want a real app on top (internal tools, field data capture, client portals) without hiring a developer
skip_if: you need heavy custom logic or a high-write consumer app: the update metering punishes exactly that shape of workload, and anything beyond the published ceilings is a quote-only conversation
honest_knock: Glide meters updates, not just seats. Your bill tracks how busy the app is rather than how many people own a licence. A write-heavy workflow can pass the included 5,000 updates and add 2 cents each without anyone changing plan. The jump from Maker to Business is also steep: $49 to $199 per month on annual billing, and the row ceiling only moves from 25k to 100k. Per Glide's partner team on 18 August 2026, those ceilings track the data source rather than the plan. 25k applies to synced spreadsheet sources whatever you pay, and the 100k+ figures belong to their Big Table source. So an upgrade alone does not lift a spreadsheet-backed app past 25k rows. The pricing page is hard to read for a reason Glide does not dispute. Asked about the Individual and Business tabs, the same team called them audience segmentation. They agreed on 18 August 2026 that the comparison tables confuse, because they never put all plans side by side. And there is a trap before any of that arithmetic applies: everything above describes the classic builder, but the free signup button on glideapps.com does not lead there. We pressed it on 7 September 2026 and landed in GlideOS, the newer AI product, which meters credits instead of updates, starts at $25 a month instead of $199, and describes its free tier only as “limited credits” with no number anywhere in the pricing page or the app. Read the classic prices, click sign up, and you are evaluating something else.

pricing.notes: (GlideOS plans and the classic Business tab re-read 2026-10-17 and unchanged; the classic Explorer and Maker amounts were not printed in the page we fetched that day and were last read 2026-09-03 in a live browser session on both tabs and both billing toggles) The classic spreadsheet-to-app builder still has a genuinely free tier: unlimited drafts, one editor, up to 25k rows. Its paid plans are unchanged, but they now live on glideapps.com/classic/pricing instead of the main pricing page. On the individual tab, Explorer starts at $19 per month billed yearly or $25 billed monthly (one app, 100 personal users, 250 updates, up to 25k rows) and Maker at $49 per month billed yearly or $60 monthly. On the business tab, Business starts at $199 per month billed yearly or $249 monthly, with unlimited apps, 30 users included, 5,000 updates and up to 100k rows. Extra users are $5 each on annual billing and $6 on monthly, and extra updates cost 2 cents each. Enterprise is quote-only. VAT is added at checkout, and Business comes with a 14-day free trial. Glide now sells two products from two pages. What glideapps.com/pricing shows today is GlideOS, the newer AI builder, on its own separate subscription, and its plan ladder was rebuilt between our August and September readings. The Free, Solo and Team tiers we recorded on 4 August 2026 are gone; as read on 3 September 2026 the ladder is Free, Basic at $25 per month, Plus at $50, Pro at $125 and a quote-only Enterprise. Free carries 2 team members, 10 projects and limited credits, with no published apps. Basic adds 100 credits, 2 published apps and 1 enabled workflow. Plus gives 250 credits, 3 team members, 5 published apps, 20 projects and 5 workflows, with credit bundles up to 10,000 a month. Pro starts at 5 team members with 500 credits, 50 credits included per member, unlimited published apps and workflows, premium integrations and the option to build with your own agent over MCP. On that reading two things had gone from the plan cards: the $10 per additional member above five, and Glide's note that annual GlideOS plans were coming. So the GlideOS prices are still monthly only. Credit top-ups are capped at one a month on Basic and two on Plus, and are unlimited on Pro and Enterprise. One caveat on the row ceilings, from Glide's own partner team on 18 August 2026. The 25k limit applies to synced spreadsheet sources regardless of plan type, and the 100k+ figures apply to their Big Table data source. So which ceiling you hit is set by where the data lives as much as by what you pay. They also confirmed the Individual and Business tabs on the pricing page are audience segmentation rather than two halves of one plan ladder. Re-read 20 November 2026 on glideapps.com/pricing and glideapps.com/classic/pricing: the GlideOS ladder (Free, Basic $25, Plus $50, Pro $125 a month, Enterprise custom) and its credit, member, project and app limits are unchanged, and Classic Business is still $199 a month billed yearly with 30 users, $5 or $6 per extra user, 5,000 updates, 2 cents per extra update and up to 100k rows. The Classic Explorer and Maker amounts were again not printed in the page source. Two things changed on the GlideOS page: the FAQ again says annual plans are coming soon, and Pro now shows its member ladder, from 500 credits with 5 members up to 5,250 credits with 100 members, without printing the price of each step. The plan table on the same reading lists team members as 2 on Free, 2 on Basic, 3 on Plus and starting at 5 on Pro. Corrected 23 November 2026, after re-reading glideapps.com/pricing, glideapps.com/classic/pricing and Glide's pricing summary for agents at glideapps.com/pricing/llms.txt. Every amount above is unchanged, and the FAQ still says annual plans are coming soon. The summary, which says it was updated in September 2026, states for Pro: "Starting at $125 per month with 5 members included. Additional members are $10 per member per month, up to 100 members." The plan card on the main page shows the member ladder without that rate, but the price of a sixth member is published after all, so our earlier line that it was not is withdrawn.

sessions.what: We already knew from their pricing pages that Glide sells two products. What we had never done is the thing a reader does: go to glideapps.com and press the free signup button. We created the account; everything after that was measured in the product.
findings: The free signup button does not lead to the product our pricing section describes. Both “Sign up” and “Get started” on glideapps.com point at os.glideapps.dev: GlideOS. We signed up and landed there. The classic builder, with the free tier of unlimited drafts, one editor and 25k rows, sits behind glideapps.com/classic, which you only reach if you already know to look for it.

The two ladders are an order of magnitude apart. Classic business pricing starts at $199 a month billed yearly; GlideOS Basic is $25 a month. Same brand, same homepage, two different products with two different price floors.

And the meter is different. Classic bills updates: 5,000 included, 2 cents each after that. GlideOS bills credits: Basic 100 a month, Plus 250, Pro 500 and upward with team size. So the “updates, not seats” warning that applies to Classic does not describe the product a new signup actually lands in.

GlideOS's free tier publishes no number. Every paid tier lists its credit allowance; the free column says “Limited credits”, alongside 2 team members and 10 projects. Nowhere in the app is there a balance, not on the dashboard, not in the account menu, not on the upgrade screen. You cannot find out what you have or what you have spent.

The AI itself is not walled off on free. From one sentence — “build a simple app to track software subscriptions” — it drew up a plan, asked a sensible clarifying question about where the data lives today, produced a working mockup and then began importing components one by one. We hit no credit wall during any of it.
